owner_sentences.sentence: Thực hiện một lượt aisef run đầu-cuối bằng CLI thật trong sandbox Linux, dùng adapter kịch bản/offline để không phát sinh phí provider.
owner_sentences.evidence: python3 -B -m aisef (check, run, run --verify) ran 6 times per X1 container in the Docker Desktop guest under bubblewrap 0.12.0; the client is a scripted Python 'opencode', the provider a loopback thread answering only the preflight (18 requests in X1, 0 in hardened, 0 spend). Four runs of my own reproduce the implementer's 88/88 + 4/4. 'Sandbox Linux' = the Docker VM + bwrap, profile X1 loosening the container's seccomp/systempaths (stated).

S1 14 checks: measured confinement before the first request, both sessions PID 1 = bwrap with confine.argv, uid 1000/caps 0/NoNewPrivs 1/HOME /aisef-home, reviewer workspace ro, work landed on main, anchor 0444, VERIFIED. Seven reviewer experiments show S1 notices an unconfined session, a writable reviewer workspace and a kept operator HOME; it does NOT notice a sessions-only writable git directory (S2 does).

owner_sentences.sentence: từ chối ghi ngoài phạm vi
owner_sentences.evidence: S2 (13 attempts): no write reached the host (controller before/after + host_has); S2c shows the same attempts succeed unconfined. Precisely: 4 EROFS, 4 ENOENT (not mounted), 4 created on a sandbox tmpfs (absent on the host), 1 permitted read. 'Refused' is literal for 4 of 13; the other outcomes are containment. S2b: 5 ways isolation cannot be given -> exit 2, stage confinement, 0 provider requests. The review made the doc state the breakdown and fixed S2 passing a mistyped path alone.

S3 (background child + SIGINT/SIGTERM-ignoring grandchild + setsid child die with the confined session; 20 ms watch 0 polls with a child after; none alive after the CLI), S3t (timeout, teardown), S3c (control: setsid child outlives the CLI, RangeEscaped). Wrong-marker experiment: the watch check fails, not vacuous.

S4 8 checks on copies: right anchor VERIFIED; wrong anchor, one stream byte, edited delivery_verdict, regenerated manifests REFUTED; original 111 entries unchanged; consistency-only limit shown as observed, not asserted.

owner_sentences.sentence: Báo đúng môi trường Docker Linux guest, cấu hình và đường mã đã chạy.
owner_sentences.evidence: environment.txt/commands.txt/result carry kernel, image id, flags, bwrap sha256, settings verbatim, argv of every step, code_path_proofs with fields. After review: the network row, the S4 entry count, the developer_committed_itself credit and the S2 outcome classes were wrong or overstated in the doc and are corrected (638c0be).

owner_sentences.sentence: Lượt này chứng minh tích hợp có cách ly; không chứng minh hiệu quả với mô hình thật.
owner_sentences.evidence: Doc 7/8: scripted model, no real opencode, no OCR, egress host/not confined, one kernel/arch, X1 loosening. Not-shown list matches the report's.

owner_sentences.sentence: Không tự tắt Docker Desktop hoặc các container dịch vụ của tôi... Giữ goe-postgres và goe-valkey hoạt động; chỉ quản lý tài nguyên riêng của chiến dịch.
owner_sentences.evidence: No docker stop/rm/kill/prune/rmi/build/pull anywhere in the launcher, driver or my commands; docker run --rm of the local image only; goe-postgres-1 and goe-valkey-1 'Up 5 hours (healthy)' before and after (docker ps).

claims.claim: 88 checks (X1) + 4 (hardened) passed in each of two runs; 0 differences
claims.note: rerun1 (11ec823), rerun3 (638c0be), rerun4 (8caebec): 11 scenarios, 88/88, hardened 4/4, compare 0 differences in checks and facts vs implementer run 1; provider 18/0.

claims.claim: negative control: S1 5/14, S2 13/17, S3 4/6 fail
claims.note: reproduced on a fresh scratch tree with the same one-line change: S1 5 fail, S2 13 fail, S3 4 fail (exit 1).

claims.claim: no product code changed (aisef/ aisef2/ identical to 3dc827b; kernel_digest afe21212...)
claims.note: git diff 3dc827b HEAD -- aisef aisef2 empty; every run's kernel_digest afe21212e1419292...

the driver's own environment.network_interfaces has 11 entries: lo (up) + nine DOWN tunnel pseudo-devices + bonding_masters; IPv4 route table empty, 3 IPv6 rows all on lo (measured, review/guest-network.txt). 'No route off the container' is true.

claims.claim: S2: writes outside the scope refused, so the denials are bubblewrap's
claims.note: 4 EROFS (refused), 4 ENOENT (not mounted), 4 created into a sandbox tmpfs (not on the host), 1 read by design. True that none reached the host and that the controls show the container would have allowed them; 'refused' is literal for 4 of 13.

claims.claim: sessions[developer].developer_committed_itself=false because the git directory is read-only to the session
claims.note: the scripted developer never runs git; false by construction. The read-only git dir is shown by S2 (EROFS), not by this field.

claims.claim: PID 1's argv equals confine.argv recomputed proves the sessions ran under the kernel's wrapper
claims.note: it is an equality with the kernel's own function: proves the wrapper was applied with those inputs, not that the argv is right. Experiment: sessions-only RW git dir -> S1 14/14 pass, S2 developer:git_directory fails. Independent proofs are the inside view, S2 and the kernel's measurement.

claims.claim: measured before the first provider request
claims.note: canary mtime is the measurement's start (58 ms before the first request in rerun1); that a failing measurement stops before any request is S2b + run.py stage order. Stated in doc 8.9.

claims.claim: a record alone does not show a session was confined (every_session_recorded_as_bwrap passes in the negative control)
claims.note: client.py builds the 'bwrap network=host' string from the confine parameter, not from what ran.

claims.claim: S2c: 10 of 11 creates succeeded; 9 on the host by the controller, the tenth caught by the kernel's tree comparison; the failure is the container's EACCES
claims.note: counted from the result; journal quote and CAPABILITY_UNRUNNABLE present.
three further runs, all identical in checks and facts; only anchors, commit ids, journal digests, timestamps, timelines differ.

claims.claim: S4 stream byte + regenerated manifest verifies without an anchor (documented limit)
claims.note: observed, VERIFIED exit 0; with the anchor REFUTED.

defects_found.what: S2 passed a mistyped/nonexistent target path on its own: any errno counted as a refusal, so only the S2c control caught it (S2 17/17 with a parent that exists nowhere).
e2e_linux.sh exited 0 whatever the containers did (it ended with print done) and never checked that TREE was the ARCHIVE/COMMIT it recorded.
defects_found.fixed_in_commit: 2cd8826 (exit status, guard), 8caebec (guard counts every non-directory entry: find -type f would refuse a tree with a symlink)

defects_found.what: doc: the container has 'lo only' - contradicted by the run's own network_interfaces (lo + nine DOWN tunnel pseudo-devices).
doc: S4 re-hashes '110 entries' - data says 111 in every run.
doc/driver label: developer_committed_itself=false credited to the git directory being read-only; it is false because the scripted developer never runs git.
doc/summary: 'writes refused' overstates - 4 of 13 S2 attempts succeeded into a sandbox tmpfs and 4 were ENOENT (not mounted); the breakdown was not reported.
doc: real/simulated lists put the loopback HTTP preflight under Real without saying its answers are scripted; argv equality and canary-before-first-request limits not stated.
docs/v2.1/SANDBOX-LINUX.md section 8 row (confined real aisef run on Linux end to end: M6, not done) and docs/v2.1/REPORT.md rows 48 and 90 become stale when this evidence is committed.

false_refusal_search.what: the review's own changes can refuse a good input: the S2 ENOENT clause and the launcher guard
false_refusal_search.result: S2 clause: all 13 real rows pass in rerun2/3/4 (ENOENT rows have host_has_the_place True; the tmpfs rows are untouched). Launcher guard: refuses a bogus COMMIT and a driver differing by one edit (exit 2, no OUT_DIR made); admits the real archive extraction; the file-count test was made symlink-safe after a two-entry tar showed find -type f (1) vs tar entries (2). Not searched: a TREE built by a tool other than git archive + tar; a non-aarch64 guest (the procps library path is aarch64).

real_vs_simulated_corrections: loopback HTTP preflight: the socket exchange is real, the provider's answers are scripted (listed under both; now explained)
developer_committed_itself false: by construction of the scripted developer, not evidence of a read-only git directory
S2 'refused': 4 refused / 4 not visible / 4 contained in a sandbox tmpfs / 1 read; the attempts are fixed lists, not model behaviour

process_notes: early JSON inspection of the implementer's evidence used bare python3 with stdin scripts (cwd the evidence directory, no stray .py files) before I switched to py.sh; nothing of the product was executed that way
the host load average reached 309 during rerun1; cause not established (other campaigns); all checks still passed

the extracted trees, their tars and the mutant copies were deleted after the runs (scratch only; each run's environment.txt names its commit, tree and archive sha256; bin/make_mutants*.py rebuild the mutants from any tree); the reviewer worktree was removed, branch v21r3/e2e-rv kept at f7f308f
remaining_risks: one kernel/arch/runtime (7.0.12-linuxkit aarch64, Docker Desktop), profile X1 loosens the container; scripted model; real opencode inside the sandbox not exercised (config, CA bundle, provider via --share-net)
S2/S3 attempts are fixed lists; ENOENT outcomes depend on the layout (the work directory is under /tmp, which the sandbox replaces with a tmpfs)
4 of 13 out-of-scope writes are absorbed silently into a sandbox tmpfs (a model sees success) - by design of --tmpfs /tmp and the root tmpfs, not refused
the session's bwrap argv is not recorded in RUN.json; the proof is from inside (and is an equality with confine.argv)
canary-before-first-request is timing evidence of the measurement's start only
